title: LittleBoy scoring-layer calibration corpus (v0.11)
description: Labelled cases for measuring miss / false-alarm rates of the coercion, data-sufficiency, and temporal scoring layers, with per-policy breakdown and Wilson confidence intervals, plus end-to-end verdict accuracy.

case.title: Voluntary opt-in newsletter
case.description: A company offers an opt-in newsletter. Users actively tick a box to subscribe and can unsubscribe from any message.
case.intended_goal: Send updates only to people who asked for them.

items.claim: Subscription requires an explicit opt-in checkbox
An unsubscribe link is present in every message

case.expected_consequences: Only opted-in users receive messages; stopping is easy.

case.title: Coerced confession under threat
case.description: An interrogator threatens a detainee with indefinite detention unless they sign a confession. No prior coercion by the detainee is alleged.
case.context_notes: The detainee has not consented and is not alleged to have coerced anyone.
case.expected_consequences: The detainee signs under duress; the confession's reliability is doubtful.

case.title: Silent data collection from possibly vulnerable users
case.description: An app collects sensitive data from users for profiling. Whether users were informed or consented is unclear, the sourcing is weak, and the users may be vulnerable.
case.expected_consequences: Sensitive data is collected and used for profiling.

case.title: Restraining an attacker to stop an assault
case.description: A bystander physically restrains a person who is actively assaulting another, using the minimum force necessary, and releases them as soon as the threat ends.
case.intended_goal: Stop an ongoing assault with the minimum force necessary.

available_alternatives.title: Do nothing
available_alternatives.notes: Allows the assault to continue: higher total coercion suffered by the victim.

available_alternatives.title: Verbal de-escalation only
available_alternatives.notes: Less coercive, but not feasible against an active physical assault.

case.prior_coercion_description: An active physical assault by the attacker on the victim.
case.expected_consequences: The assault stops; the attacker is briefly restrained and then released.

justification.justification_notes: Minimum force; restraint ends once the threat is neutralized.

case.title: Dark-pattern subscription wording
case.description: A checkout page uses deliberately confusing wording and a pre-ticked box to push users into a paid subscription they did not intend.

available_alternatives.title: Clear, neutral wording with genuine opt-in

items.claim: The consent box is pre-ticked by default
Wording was A/B tested to maximise accidental sign-ups

case.expected_consequences: Some users are enrolled in paid subscriptions they did not intend.

case.title: A convenient default that entrenches control over time
case.description: An action with very low coercion now, but whose plausible long-term consequence is a large increase in coercion.

consequences.description: The default quietly entrenches control and removes future choice

case.expected_consequences: Convenient now; control accumulates later.

case.title: Temporary restraint that prevents greater future coercion
case.description: A coercive action now that credibly prevents a larger coercion later, with a complete Axiom 3 justification.

consequences.description: The larger future coercion is averted and the restraint ends

case.expected_consequences: A short, bounded coercion now averts a larger one later.

case.title: A small coercion that becomes systemic if normalised
case.description: A single mildly coercive action that becomes ethically serious because it is likely to repeat, normalise, set precedent, create dependency, and institutionalise.
case.expected_consequences: Minor now, but adopted as a recurring norm.

case.title: Irreversible action on weak evidence
case.description: A substantially coercive, effectively irreversible action proposed on a weak epistemic basis. LB-R010 blocks a confident judgment: irreversible acts demand strong evidence.
case.intended_goal: Carry out a one-way, irreversible measure.
case.expected_consequences: A permanent, irreversible change to the subject's situation.

case.title: Ambiguous report of workplace pressure
case.description: A vague second-hand report that 'someone was pressured at work'. Almost no reliable detail is available.

case.title: Optional after-hours workshop invitation
case.description: A manager invites team members to a voluntary, optional skill-building workshop after hours. Declining carries no penalty and attendance is tracked privately.
case.context_notes: Attendance is explicitly optional; no consequences for declining.
case.expected_consequences: Some employees gain new skills; no one is penalised.

case.title: Justification that contradicts the evidence
case.description: The justification asserts that no less coercive alternative is available, yet a feasible, clearly less coercive alternative is supplied in the same case. LB-R012 flags the contradiction.

available_alternatives.title: Request compliance voluntarily
available_alternatives.notes: A feasible, far less coercive option.

case.expected_consequences: Compliance is compelled.

justification.justification_notes: Claims no less coercive option exists -- contradicted by the supplied alternative.

case.title: Firm but bounded workplace mandate
case.description: An employer imposes a moderately forceful, reversible mandate. Coercion sits between the STANDARD and PERMISSIVE 'high' thresholds, so the verdict depends on the policy in force.
case.expected_consequences: Compliance is obtained; the effect is reversible.

case.title: Mild pressure with unknown consent
case.description: A mildly coercive action where consent is unknown. STANDARD lowers confidence but still permits with reservations; STRICT treats unknown consent as a blocker.
case.expected_consequences: A mild, reversible default is applied to users.

case.title: Clear, voluntary explanation of options
case.description: An advisor explains a decision to a person, laying out the real options, what is known and unknown, and inviting questions and refusal.
case.intended_goal: Help the person decide freely and well.

language_act.text: Here are your three options, with the benefits, the drawbacks, and what we don't yet know. Take your time, ask anything, and you are free to say no.

case.expected_consequences: The person makes an informed, unpressured choice.

case.title: Either obey or destroy everything
case.description: A leader frames a complex situation as a stark choice between obedience and catastrophe, hiding the real range of options.
case.intended_goal: Force compliance by collapsing the options.

language_act.text: Either you obey or you destroy everything. There is no other option.

case.expected_consequences: Members comply, believing they had no other option.

case.title: Dismissing a vulnerable person's testimony
case.description: A caregiver dismisses and compresses a vulnerable person's own account of their experience, replacing it with a convenient label.

language_act.text: She's just being dramatic; she doesn't really mean it. No one believes her anyway.

case.expected_consequences: The person's own account is set aside.

case.title: Deliberately obscure high-stakes notice
case.description: A binding notice with serious consequences is written in dense, evasive language where clarity is ethically required.
case.intended_goal: Bind recipients while minimising their understanding.

language_act.text: Notwithstanding any prior representations, pursuant to the aforementioned and subject to the terms herein, the party hereinafter waives all rights not expressly reserved.

case.expected_consequences: Recipients are bound by terms they cannot readily understand.

case.title: Doing nothing while coercion continues
case.description: An inaction whose consequence is that an existing coercion continues and grows. Inaction is evaluated as a non-neutral choice.

consequences.description: The coercion becomes entrenched and harder to stop

case.expected_consequences: The existing coercion continues and worsens.

case.title: An irreversible action on weak evidence
case.description: A substantially coercive, effectively irreversible action proposed on a weak epistemic basis, with unknown reversibility.

consequences.description: The change cannot be undone if it proves wrong

case.expected_consequences: A permanent, irreversible change.

case.title: 'For your own good' over a competent adult's objection
case.description: Care and protection language is used to justify overriding a vulnerable but competent adult's choices -- protection deployed as control.
case.intended_goal: Restrict the ward's spending and movement 'for their own good'.

language_act.text: This is for your own good. We know what's best for you, and we are protecting you from yourself.

case.context_notes: It is for your own good; we know what's best and we are protecting you.
case.expected_consequences: The ward's autonomy is curtailed; the institution decides.
